Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: 48-year-old man with acute self-limited watery diarrhoea, initial vomiting, subjective low-grade fever, dehydration, no red-flag features (blood, severe pain). No recent antibiotics or travel; no sick contacts identified.  

Differential diagnoses (consistent with transcript):  
• Viral gastroenteritis (high likelihood) – classic abrupt onset, short course, vomiting then diarrhoea, expected spontaneous resolution.  
• Bacterial food-borne gastroenteritis (moderate likelihood) – similar timeframe; less supportive evidence (no abdominal cramps, no high-risk meal identified).  
• Clostridioides difficile infection (low likelihood) – lacks antibiotic exposure.  

Working diagnosis: Presumed viral gastroenteritis.  

Management priorities: Symptomatic relief, prevent dehydration, advise time off work until 24–48 h symptom-free, safety-net instructions to return if symptoms persist/worsen.

Management Plan

- Encourage high oral fluid intake; recommend oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte).  
- Paracetamol as needed for fever or malaise – dose not specified.  
- Rest and remain off work for next 1–2 days; may return when diarrhoea-free for 24–48 h.  
- Safety-net: review if no improvement within one week, if develops blood in stool, persistent vomiting, high fever, or worsening dehydration.  
- No medications prescribed; no investigations ordered at this stage.  
- Follow-up: telephone or in-person review if indicated.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

1. Viral gastroenteritis – High likelihood; abrupt onset, vomiting followed by 3-day watery diarrhoea, self-limiting course.  
2. Bacterial food-borne gastroenteritis (Salmonella/Campylobacter/ETEC) – Moderate likelihood; overlapping presentation but less systemic upset reported.
